function: CSI compression and feedback: UE encoder compresses the downlink CSI matrix, BS decoder reconstructs it, in FDD massive MIMO (p. 2).
system: Massive MIMO FDD downlink, BS with n antennas, single-antenna UEs, no RIS; COST 2100 indoor 5.3 GHz and outdoor 300 MHz (pp. 2, 4).
method: Supervised deep encoder-decoder CNN with cosine criss-cross attention and 1D convolutions; MSE plus VGG-19 perceptual loss (pp. 2-4).
data_channel: COST 2100 dataset, indoor 5.3 GHz and outdoor 300 MHz scenarios; no train/test split stated (p. 4).
test_conditions: Results reported separately for indoor and outdoor scenarios at compression ratios 1/4 to 1/64; no testing on unseen scenario, band or configuration (p. 4).
baselines: Learned only: CsiNet, CRNet, CLNet, CsiNet+, ACRNet, TransNet; no classical method; CSI-StripeFormer not compared as too heavy (p. 4).
metrics: NMSE in dB, FLOPs, and parameters (Tables I and II, p. 4).
complexity: FLOPs per method in Table I (HCC-Net 35.21M at ratio 1/4); FLOPs and parameters of ablated variants in Table II (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "the COST 2100 dataset introduced in [20] is used in our experiments" - COST 2100 is a listed standard model.
q2_support: p. 4: "an indoor 5.3GHz scenario and an outdoor 300MHz scenario" - each scenario is evaluated on its own in Table I; no model trained on one scenario or configuration and tested on another is reported.
q3_support: p. 4: "CsiNet+ [18], ACRNet [19], TransNet [4]" - Table I compares only with learned networks (also CsiNet, CRNet, CLNet); no non-learned baseline appears anywhere in the paper.
q4_support: p. 4: "in terms of both NMSE and FLOPs" - Table I reports the FLOPs of every method and Table II adds the number of parameters.
q5_support: p. 4: "the COST 2100 dataset introduced in [20] is used in our experiments" - named shared CSI benchmark dataset; the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Included, area 2 (CSI feedback, FDD massive MIMO, BS with n antennas). Tables I to III were read from the page images (pp. 4-5). q5 is a judgment for the reviewer to confirm: the paper names the COST 2100 dataset but gives no link and never says it is public; the mark rests on that CSI benchmark being publicly shared. Table II row 'HCC-Net (ours)' (CCA only, 24.59M FLOPs, -32.43 dB) differs from the Table I HCC-Net row (35.21M, -34.29 dB); the Table II row 'without Perceptual loss' has 35.21M FLOPs.
